title: Bracket misalignment at assembly
short: A deformed retaining bracket stopped a pilot dishwasher build. Scan-to-CAD and tolerance stack-up data supported the drawing revisions that cut the assembly failure rate from 3% to 0.5%.
lede: A pilot dishwasher build hit a no-build condition when a bracket that retains a critical component arrived deformed. I supported the investigation with scan-to-CAD inspection data and tolerance stack-up studies.
ownership: I supported the root-cause investigation. My part was the dimensional analysis and tolerance stack-up studies on the affected assembly and its surrounding components, and presenting the scan and tolerance data to engineering. The findings supported the drawing revisions that followed; the revisions themselves were a team outcome.

sections.heading: Problem and constraints
paras: A pilot dishwasher build encountered an assembly error: a deformed bracket retaining a critical component created a **no-build condition**. The objective was to identify the root cause and contributing factors, and to prevent the failure from recurring.

figures.alt: A deformed sheet-metal retaining bracket photographed on a plain background.
figures.caption: The deformed bracket from the pilot build.

sections.heading: Approach
paras: In an assembly like this, each part's dimensional variation stacks with that of its mating parts. A scan-to-CAD comparison shows where real parts depart from nominal geometry, and a tolerance stack-up shows how much of that departure the assembly can absorb before a part no longer seats.
bullets: Took a random sample of **15 parts** to evaluate shipping behavior.
Used PolyWorks 3D scan-to-CAD analysis to compare the physical parts against nominal CAD, using datums, surface profile, perpendicularity, and concentricity.
Ran dimensional analysis and tolerance stack-up studies on the affected assembly and the surrounding components.

sections.heading: Verification
paras: Scans at the initial condition and at resolution were checked against the same drawing callout: a surface profile of 0.035 to datums A, B and C. The initial scan shows the bracket outside that tolerance and tilted away from its nominal 90 degree angle; the resolution scan is within it.

figures.alt: PolyWorks inspection view of a bent sheet-metal bracket overlaid on its nominal CAD, with a red Surface Profile 2 report showing a measured value of 0.183 and a Z angle of 84.741 degrees against 90.000 nominal.
figures.caption: Initial scan. Surface profile 0.183 against the 0.035 callout (fail); Z angle 84.741 against 90.000 nominal.

figures.alt: PolyWorks inspection view of the bracket at resolution, with a Surface Profile 2 report showing a measured value of 0.017 and a Z angle of 89.352 degrees against 90.000 nominal.
figures.caption: Resolution scan. Surface profile 0.017 (pass); Z angle 89.352 against 90.000 nominal.

sections.heading: Results
bullets: Presented the scan and tolerance data in a simplified engineering review to communicate the failure mechanism and root cause.
The findings supported drawing revisions that reduced assembly failures from 3% to 0.5%, contributing to approximately $150K in savings.
The work also supported broader hardware evaluation, qualification testing, and engineering validation for cost, quality, and product performance improvements.

tools: GD&T: datums, surface profile, perpendicularity, concentricity
note: Figures and numbers are as presented in my reviewed and approved portfolio catalog. Savings are approximate and reported, not independently audited.
